title: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
subtitle: Why Muslims love Al-Aqsa and seek justice for Palestine
summary: Palestine matters to Muslims for two connected reasons: Al-Aqsa is a blessed sanctuary named in the Quran and honored by the Prophet, and Islam commands believers to stand for justice and human dignity. Sacred love should lead to worship, truthful advocacy, mercy, and care for people—not hatred or collective blame.

sections.title: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
sections.body: Muslims care about Palestine because a sacred place and a human responsibility meet there. Al-Aqsa holds a central place in Muslim worship and memory. Palestinians are also people whose lives, homes, worship, and dignity matter. Islam joins these concerns without denying anyone else's humanity or grief.

sections.title: A Blessed Sanctuary
sections.body:
Quran 17:1 says that Allah took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to al-Masjid al-Aqsa—the Farthest Mosque—whose surroundings He blessed. The verse names Al-Aqsa but does not use the city-name Jerusalem. Authentic hadith identifies the destination as Bayt al-Maqdis, Jerusalem: [Sahih al-Bukhari 3886](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3886) records that the city was shown to the Prophet when his opponents questioned the journey.

The Prophet also named Al-Aqsa among the three mosques for which a special journey of worship is undertaken ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1189](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1189)). [Sahih Muslim 525b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:525b) records that the early Muslims faced Jerusalem in their prayer direction, or qiblah, for sixteen or seventeen months before it changed to the Kaaba. These texts, not a modern political slogan, are the foundation of Muslim love for Al-Aqsa. The detailed article on [Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa](/articles/jerusalem-and-al-aqsa) explains the narrations and sanctuary terms further.

sections.title: Sacred Love Creates Human Responsibility
sections.body:
A mosque cannot be honored while the dignity of people is ignored. Quran 5:8 commands believers not to let hatred make them unjust. That rule applies even when anger and grief are intense. Muslims should oppose oppression, protect innocent life, verify claims, and refuse anti-Jewish, anti-Christian, or anti-Muslim hatred.

Quran 22:40 speaks of people driven from their homes and names monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques among places where God's name is remembered. The verse is not a modern legal ruling about Jerusalem. It gives a moral vision in which resisting wrongful expulsion and protecting worship are connected.

sections.title: A Dawah Shown Through Worship and Justice
sections.body:
Palestine gives Muslims an opportunity to show what submission to Allah should produce: prayer without idolatry, courage without cruelty, compassion without dishonesty, and justice without collective blame. Caring for Palestinians should include lawful aid, careful learning, truthful speech, and prayer.

This conduct invites people to see Islam not as a tribal identity but as worship of the one God expressed through mercy and moral responsibility.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
sections.body: Palestine matters to Muslims because Allah blessed the surroundings of Al-Aqsa, the Prophet honored the mosque, and Islamic ethics requires justice for people. Muslims should love Al-Aqsa, support the oppressed through lawful and truthful means, protect innocent life, and reject hatred and falsehood.

quranVerses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْأَقْصَا ٱلَّذِى بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ
quranVerses.translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quranVerses.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
